title: Decision cache eviction and telemetry harmonization for smart router
creator: Asha Patel
body:
Background:
The smart routing layer maintains an in-memory decision cache that speeds up frequent route evaluations (policy decisions, region affinity, and fallback targets). Over time the cache has grown complex: multiple eviction heuristics, fragmented TTLs, and divergent metric labels across callers. This causes: stale decisions during capacity churn, uneven memory pressure across pods, and noisy/duplicated telemetry that makes incident diagnosis slow.

Scope and Goals:
1) Replace the ad-hoc eviction rules with a single, configurable LRU+LRU-TTL hybrid that:
   - prioritizes short-lived hot keys (keeps them in LRU order)
   - enforces a global soft-memory limit per router instance and a hard limit fallback
   - exposes eviction diagnostics (counts, victim keys sampling)
2) Harmonize telemetry and tracing for all routing decisions: consistent metric names, tags (model, region, route_group, priority_tier), and a single trace span pattern for decision evaluation.
3) Introduce a migration plan that keeps correctness and performance during the rollout: toggleable feature-flag, canary per region, and automatic rollback on SLO regressions.
4) Upgrade routing-proto to v3.0 to pick up compact decision encoding (backwards-compatible) and bump metrics-lib to 2.0 which provides batch counter increments and improved histograms.

Constraints and Trade-offs:
- We cannot increase tail latency for 99th pctiles during rollout; any added eviction computation must be O(1) amortized.
- Memory limits differ between Dedicated and Hosted nodes; config must support both.
- Metrics-lib 2.0 changes bucket semantics; harmonization requires re-baselining dashboards.

Design Summary:
- Cache implementation: a modular cache with two tiers: hot-LRU (fast path, lock-free ring buffer) and warm-TTL (sharded small maps with per-shard expirations). A global approximate size counter (atomic) enforces soft limit. When soft limit exceeded, evict from warm tier first; if still over, evict LRU hot entries. Eviction is logged via sampling (1/1000) and a counter.
- API: cache.GetDecision(key) returns DecisionContext + source_tag (cache_hit|miss|stale) and exposes lineage metadata for tracing.
- Telemetry: adopt metric names: routing.decision.evaluation.latency_ms, routing.decision.cache.hit, routing.decision.cache.eviction.count, routing.decision.fallback.triggered. Tags: model, region, route_group, reason. Traces: span name routing.evaluate with attributes decision.key, cache_status, duration_ms.
- Migration: feature flag router_cache_v2 with rollout steps: off -> canary in eu-west -> 5% traffic us-east -> 25% -> 100% if no regressions. A health-check job runs microbenchmarks every 30 minutes comparing old and new path for throughput/latency and compares telemetry baselines.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Unit and integration tests cover cache correctness, eviction invariants, and multi-threaded access.
- No regression in P50/P95/P99 latency on canary for 1 hour under synthetic load.
- Dashboards updated with new metric names and alerts adjusted for metrics-lib 2.0 semantics.
- PRs merged for routing-proto v3.0 and metrics-lib 2.0 upgrade with compatibility shims where needed.

Implementation Plan (high-level):
1) Prototype cache module in router/decision/cache_v2 with feature flag disabled. Add unit tests and microbench harness.
2) Add harmonized metric emitters and trace span helpers in router/telemetry package.
3) Upgrade dependencies in a separate PR, add compatibility adapters for metrics bucket changes.
4) Run integration canary in eu-west (one pod pool) for 48h with regression checks.
5) Gradual rollout with automated rollback on SLO breach or increased error rate.
6) Cleanup: remove old cache paths and legacy metric names after 2 cycles.

Risks and Mitigations:
- Risk: metrics-lib 2.0 leads to histogram bucket drift -> Mitigation: run side-by-side telemetry for 3 days and maintain both names with migration tags until baseline established.
- Risk: eviction policy causes thrashing under spiky workloads -> Mitigation: conservative default soft limits and enable adaptive backoff that temporarily increases TTL for hot keys under high churn.
- Risk: feature-flag complexity -> Mitigation: central rollout orchestration in console with canary gating and retry windows.

Rollout Signals and Monitoring:
- Primary signals: routing.decision.evaluation.latency_ms P95/P99, routing.decision.cache.hit rate, system memory pressure per router pod, fallback invocation rate.
- Secondary signals: trace duration distributions and sampled eviction logs.
- Rollback thresholds: +20% P99 latency or +15% fallback invocation sustained for 10 minutes triggers auto-rollback.

- Benchmark dashboard (canary): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/routing/cache-v2-canary

updates: 2026-03-01: Ticket created. Initial problem statement and high-level plan (Asha).
2026-03-03: Spike completed comparing LRU vs TTL hybrids; LRU+TTL chosen for workload mix (Daniel).
2026-03-05: Prototype cache_v2 added behind feature flag. Benchmarks show 8% lower P99 under steady load but 5% memory increase (microbench results attached).
2026-03-08: Telemetry harmonization spec reviewed by Observability team. Agreed on metric names and tags (Sofia).
2026-03-10: routing-proto v3.0 upgrade PR opened; compat tests added. Canary gating plan drafted.
2026-03-12: Canary started in eu-west with 2 pods. Early telemetry stable; monitoring alerts configured to auto-rollback on thresholds.
